New site? Copy the [starter](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/tree/main/starter) instead -- it has the extension installed. This page is for adding the library to a site you already have.

mathviz ships two ways from one source tree. Both give you the same `window.VM`, the same CSS, and the same behaviour.

## Quarto site, book or document

```sh
quarto add apurvanakade/mathviz@v0.1.13
```

This copies the extension into `_extensions/apurvanakade/mathviz/` in your project. Enable it project-wide in `_quarto.yml`, or per page in front matter:

```yaml
filters:
  - mathviz
```

The filter puts math.js and Plotly (from a CDN, pinned to the versions the library is tested against), then `mathviz.js` and `mathviz.css` (served from your own `site_libs/`), into every HTML page's `<head>`.

### Options

All optional, under a `mathviz:` key in `_quarto.yml` or a page's front matter:

```yaml
mathviz:
  plotly: false             # your pages draw with D3/canvas/Plot -- skip Plotly
  mathjs: false             # ...or math.js. Either also accepts a URL string
  css: false                # bring your own stylesheet
  referrer: same-origin     # emit <meta name="referrer"> ahead of the CDN tags
```

| Key | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `plotly` | `true` (default), `false`, or a URL | Whether to add the Plotly tag, and from where. With `false` the Plotly patch is a silent no-op and the `VM.plotting` theme functions still work for Observable Plot. |
| `mathjs` | `true` (default), `false`, or a URL | Whether to add the math.js tag, and from where. `VM.expressions.*` take the instance as an argument, so a page that loads math.js another way passes that. |
| `css` | `true` (default) or `false` | Whether to add `mathviz.css`. With `false` you supply the `--vm-*` tokens and the `ojs-*` rules yourself -- see [Theming](theming.qmd). |
| `referrer` | a [referrer policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta/name/referrer) string | Emits `<meta name="referrer" content="…">` **before** the CDN tags, so the third-party origins don't see a page's path or query string -- which on a math page is the reader's own input. Visual Math Lab uses `same-origin`. |

Further keys turn on self-hosted fonts and site-wide chrome (a sidebar rail, embedding, a Share button, a Report bug popup, a phone notice), and the extension ships an optional Quarto theme. All are off by default -- see [Site extras](site.qmd).

### Versions and updating

```sh
quarto update apurvanakade/mathviz@v0.1.13    # move to a release
quarto add apurvanakade/mathviz@v0.1.13       # pin at install time
```

Always name the tag. Without one (or with `@latest`), Quarto installs the `main` branch, which can be ahead of the last release.

To stay on the latest release without thinking about it, run the [site kit](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/tree/main/kit)'s `update-mathviz.sh` as a `pre-render` hook. It updates the extension before each render and keeps the installed copy when you're offline.

### Adding your own functions

A site that needs functions mathviz doesn't have can keep them in a second, local extension that loads after mathviz and adds to the same `VM`. The [site kit](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/tree/main/kit) has the template: copy it in and add `mathviz-local` after `mathviz` under `filters:`. It is laid out like mathviz's own source, so a function other sites could use can go upstream as a pull request.

## Any other web page

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/apurvanakade/mathviz@v0.1.13/dist/mathviz.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjs@15.2.0/lib/browser/math.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-2.35.2.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/apurvanakade/mathviz@v0.1.13/dist/mathviz.js"></script>
```

- Load **Plotly before `mathviz.js`**. If Plotly arrives later (a dynamic import), call [`VM.plotting.installPlotlyPatch()`](reference/plotting.qmd#installPlotlyPatch) yourself.
- Pin the tag in the URL. jsDelivr also serves `@main`, but a tag is what you can reason about.
- Without Quarto and Observable Inputs, some CSS has nothing to attach to; [Internals](reference/internals.qmd#host-markup) says what degrades and what doesn't.
